12. ReDoS — PARTIAL (1 finding, LOW)
==========================================================================
Audited every regex in src/:

------------------------------------------------------------------------
SEC-07-REDO-1  (LOW)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
File  : src/app/api/contact/route.ts:28
Code  :
  const spamPatterns = [
    /\b(viagra|cialis|casino|lottery|prize|winner|bitcoin investment)\b/,
    /(https?:\/\/[^\s]+){3,}/,   // ← THIS ONE
    /(.)\1{10,}/,
  ];
Issue: `/(https?:\/\/[^\s]+){3,}/` — quantified greedy group `(...){3,}`
  where the inner `[^\s]+` matches one or more non-whitespace chars.
  For pathological input `http://xxxxxx...x` (single URL, no spaces,
  length N), the regex needs 3+ matches. After the first `http://`
  matches and `[^\s]+` consumes all N chars, the engine tries to match
  a 2nd `http://` — fails — backtracks `[^\s]+` to N-1 chars — tries
  2nd `http://` — fails — backtracks to N-2 — and so on. O(N²) worst
  case. With the message cap of 5000 chars (contact/route.ts:67
  `message.slice(0, 5000)`) → ~25M ops → ~250ms on V8. Single-request
  CPU spike, but rate-limited (8 req / 15 min / IP).
PoC:
  # Build a 5000-char single-URL payload:
  MSG="http://$(python3 -c 'print("x"*4960)')"
  # Then:
  curl -s -X POST https://victim.com/api/contact \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{
      \"name\":\"x\",\"email\":\"x@x.com\",
      \"message\":\"$MSG\",
      \"recaptchaToken\":\"<valid-token>\",
      \"_t\":0
    }"
  # Single request burns ~250ms CPU. With a valid reCAPTCHA token
  # required (mandatory at line 87), this is hard to scale.
  # Attacker needs many valid reCAPTCHA tokens — each requires solving
  # a CAPTCHA. Cost-prohibitive at scale.
Severity: LOW (mitigated by reCAPTCHA + 8/15min rate limit + 5000-char
  cap; ~250ms CPU per request is below typical DoS threshold).

------------------------------------------------------------------------
Other regexes audited (all SAFE):
------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - src/lib/sanitize-embed.ts:19  `/<iframe[^>]*>/i`       — bounded by `>`
  - src/lib/sanitize-embed.ts:25  `/src=["']([^"']*)["']/i`— bounded by `"'`
  - src/app/api/track/route.ts:16 `/bot|crawl|spider|slurp/i` — literal alt
  - src/app/api/contact/route.ts:27 `/\b(viagra|...|bitcoin investment)\b/` — literal alt

  - src/app/api/contact/route.ts:43 `/bot|crawl|...|curl/i` — literal alt

  - src/app/page.tsx:334            (same email regex)    — bounded

==========================================================================
FINAL VERDICT
==========================================================================
No CRITICAL or HIGH injection vulnerabilities found in src/.

The codebase is well-defended against the classic injection categories:
SQL injection (Prisma-only, no raw queries), NoSQL (n/a — only SQLite),
prototype pollution (no Object.assign, no lodash, Object.fromEntries is
safe), path traversal (no fs APIs except static db path), LDAP (none),
XML/XXE (no XML parsing), template injection (no template engines, no
eval/Function, sanitizeEmbed + CSP defense holds).

The remaining gaps are:
  (a) 4 admin-gated SSRF endpoints (LLM baseUrl, bot tokens, forward
       email) with no host/scheme allowlist. MEDIUM.
  (b) 4 mass-assignment endpoints (equipment, content, themes, nav)
       using `{ ...body.data }` spread without field allowlist on
       create/update. MEDIUM.
  (c) 1 latent SQL injection in scripts/reset-admin-password.sh:50
       (already known as F-22). LOW.
  (d) 2 JSON.parse sites on admin-stored LabEquipment.specs that
       enable a public-side 500-DoS once an admin stores bad JSON. LOW.
  (e) 1 ReDoS in /api/contact spam filter (mitigated by reCAPTCHA +
       rate limit). LOW.

All MEDIUM findings require an admin session to exploit. Combined with
the prior audit's CRITICAL (F-2 default admin123) and HIGH (F-NEW-1
password fallback backdoor — though V17.2.1-FINAL claims the password
fallback was removed, line 4 of admin-auth.ts confirms: "V17.2: حذف
password fallback" — so the F-NEW-1 backdoor IS closed in the current
code), an attacker who gains admin via F-2 (default password) can
pivot to SSRF / mass-assignment / stored-XSS via MA-4 (NavItem href).

Recommendation: address SEC-07-MA-4 first (closes stored-XSS on every
visitor), then SEC-07-SSRF-2 (closes bot-token SSRF that exfils
future visitor PII), then the remaining SSRF / MA / JSON / ReDoS
items in priority order above.

10. Are there accessibility issues?
    ⚠️ YES — multiple issues found.

    A. MISSING: Skip-to-content link
       - No `<a href="#main" class="skip-link">Skip to content</a>` anywhere
         in page.tsx:414-878. Keyboard users must tab through entire navbar
         + status bar on every page load. WCAG 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks).

    B. Theme buttons (page.tsx:510-516) — color-only, no accessible name:
       - Each button contains only `<span className="theme-icon">` (a
         colored dot). No text content. `title` attribute is present but
         NOT reliably announced by screen readers.
       - WCAG 1.4.1 (Use of Color): color is the ONLY means of conveying
         theme identity.
       - WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value): no accessible name.
       - Fix: add `aria-label={...}` to each button.

    C. Hamburger button (page.tsx:530-536) — missing aria-expanded:
       - Has `aria-label="Toggle menu"` ✅
       - Missing `aria-expanded={menuOpen}` and `aria-controls="nav-links"`.
       - Screen reader users cannot tell if menu is open or closed.
       - WCAG 4.1.2.

    D. Tutorial modal (page.tsx:840-874) — missing dialog semantics:
       - No `role="dialog"`, no `aria-modal="true"`, no `aria-labelledby`.
       - Modal title (line 845) is a `<span className="tutorial-modal-bar-title">`,
         not a heading. Should be `<h2>` for proper heading hierarchy.
       - No focus trap: when modal opens, focus stays on the clicked
         tutorial card. Tab key can move focus to elements BEHIND the
         modal (page.tsx:286-289 only locks body scroll, not focus).
       - No focus return: when modal closes, focus is not returned to
         the triggering element.
       - WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order), 2.4.7 (Focus Visible on close).

    E. Footer admin link (page.tsx:819-826) — non-interactive anchor:
       - `<a className="footer-admin" title="Ctrl+Shift+A">` has NO href,
         no role="button", no tabindex, no onClick.
       - Keyboard users cannot focus or activate it.
       - The title suggests it opens via Ctrl+Shift+A keyboard shortcut,
         but the element itself is dead for keyboard users.
       - WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard).

    F. Nav links (page.tsx:484-494) — missing aria-current:
       - No `aria-current="true"` on the link matching the current scroll
         position. Screen reader users navigating the nav get no indication
         of which section is in view.
       - Minor; WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships).

    G. Reveal-on-scroll (page.tsx:267-283) — visibility for AT:
       - Elements with `data-reveal` start hidden (CSS `reveal` class) and
         become visible (`.reveal.visible`) when scrolled into view via
         IntersectionObserver.
       - If CSS uses `visibility: hidden` (not just opacity), AT may not
         announce these elements until scrolled. If only opacity is used,
         AT announces them regardless. Cannot verify without reading
         personal.css reveal class — but this is a common a11y trap.
       - The IntersectionObserver runs ONCE on mount (line 267-283) with
         empty dep array `[]` — if content loads asynchronously from DB
         (useContent), newly rendered reveal elements are NOT observed.
         BUG: skills/books/articles/tutorials cards that render AFTER the
         observer effect ran will never reveal. This is both a
         functional bug AND an a11y issue (content stuck invisible).

    H. Status bar (page.tsx:437-461) — decorative dot has no text alt:
       - line 440: `<span className="dot"></span>` — green dot indicator
         with no text alternative. Sighted users see "online" + green dot;
         AT users hear only "online". Acceptable since text conveys the
         meaning.

    I. Form (page.tsx:762-804):
       - Labels: page.tsx:775, 779, 783 — `htmlFor` properly associated
         with `id` on name/email/message inputs. ✅
       - page.tsx:787 — `<label>` for "Robot check" has NO `htmlFor` (no
         input id to associate with; the reCAPTCHA is a div). Acceptable
         but the label is not programmatically linked.
       - page.tsx:803 — `<p role="status">` for form errors ✅ live region.
       - page.tsx:800 — submit button has no `aria-busy` when submitting.
         Visual cue only (text changes to "Sending..."). Minor.
       - page.tsx:762 — `noValidate` disables browser validation; relies
         on JS validation in handleSubmit. If JS fails, form cannot
         submit at all. Acceptable for SPA.

    J. Heading hierarchy:
       - h1: page.tsx:546 (hero-title) — single h1 ✅
       - h2: section titles (about, skills, books, articles, tutorials,
         contact) — multiple h2s ✅
       - h2: page.tsx:426 (DevTools warning) — appears in overlay, may
         confuse hierarchy if rendered alongside main h2s.
       - h1: page.tsx:148 (Domain Setup Required) — replaces body, so
         only one h1 exists at a time. ✅
       - h3: page.tsx:595 (about-card facts title), 630 (skill-card
         category) — proper nesting. ✅
       - ⚠️ page.tsx:845 (tutorial modal title) — is a `<span>`, not a
         heading. Should be h2 or h3.

    K. Iframes:
       - page.tsx:852-870 — tutorial iframe has `title` ✅
       - reCAPTCHA iframe (runtime-injected by grecaptcha) — title set
         by Google's script, not controllable here.

    L. HTML lang/dir:
       - page.tsx:107-108 — sets `document.documentElement.lang` and
         `dir` on mount. ✅
       - But initial server render: lang/dir come from layout.tsx (not
         audited). If layout has hardcoded `lang="en"`, FA users get
         wrong lang until client effect runs. Hydration mismatch risk
         (noted as already fixed in worklog V18.4:31-32 via
         suppressHydrationWarning).

    M. prefers-reduced-motion:
       - personal.css:1381, 1449, 3473 — `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:
         reduce)` rules exist ✅
       - But page.tsx:299 `behavior: "smooth"` on scrollTo is NOT gated
         by reduced-motion preference. Minor.

    N. Color contrast:
       - Cannot audit without rendering; depends on theme CSS variables.
       - page.tsx:702 `color: "var(--text-faint)"` on "No clips yet."
         text — if --text-faint is too faint, contrast may fail WCAG

■ FEAT-12-A | MEDIUM | Unused imports (dead code / bundle bloat)
  Files: src/app/page.tsx:12-18
  Issue: 5 components imported but NEVER rendered in the homepage JSX:
    - ContentManager      (line 12)
    - ThemeBuilder         (line 15)
    - TextEditor          (line 16)
    - NavMenuManager      (line 17)
    - AccessUserManager   (line 18)
  These are admin-panel components, likely used in /admin or /dashboard
  routes. Importing them in page.tsx pulls their code into the homepage
  client bundle (Next.js does not tree-shake unused named imports from
  "use client" files reliably). Increases TTI for homepage visitors.
  Fix: remove the 5 imports from page.tsx; move them to the admin
  page that actually renders them.

■ FEAT-12-B | MEDIUM | Dead captcha state (orphaned code)
  Files: src/app/page.tsx:67, 373-381
  Issue: `const [captcha, setCaptcha] = useState({ q: "1 + 1", a: 2 });`
  is declared at line 67 and regenerated on successful form submit
  (lines 373-381 generate a new math captcha), but:
    - `captcha.q` is NEVER rendered in the form JSX (lines 762-804).
    - `captcha.a` is NEVER validated in handleSubmit (lines 316-398).
  The form uses Google reCAPTCHA (lines 786-798) for bot detection
  instead. The math-captcha state and its regeneration logic are dead
  code — confusing for maintainers and a latent bug if someone wires it
  up incorrectly later.
  Fix: delete lines 67 and 373-381.

■ FEAT-12-C | HIGH | IntersectionObserver runs once; DB-rendered cards never reveal
  Files: src/app/page.tsx:267-283
  Issue: The reveal-on-scroll useEffect has an empty dependency array
  `[]` (line 283), so it runs ONCE on mount. At mount time,
  `useContent` (line 56) returns the fallback empty arrays (useContent.ts:17-27)
  because the /api/content fetch (useContent.ts:42) is async. By the
  time the fetch resolves and skills/books/articles/tutorials cards
  render (lines 624, 647, 665, 681), the IntersectionObserver has
  already finished its initial sweep and will NOT observe the new
  elements.
  Result: ALL ArchiveGrid cards (books, articles, tutorials) and ALL
  skill cards (page.tsx:629 `data-reveal={`skill-${i}`}`) that come
  from the DB will remain in the `reveal` (hidden) state until the
  user scrolls past them — but since they were never observed, even
  scrolling won't trigger reveal. They stay invisible.
  This is both a FUNCTIONAL bug (content invisible to sighted users)
  and an A11Y bug (content not announced to AT if CSS uses
  visibility:hidden).
  Fix: add `contentLoading` or `siteContent.skills.length` etc. to the
  useEffect dependency array so it re-runs when DB content arrives.

■ FEAT-12-D | MEDIUM | Theme type union duplicated
  Files: src/app/page.tsx:70, 113
  Issue: The theme type `"terminal" | "clean" | "midnight" | "amber" |
  "cyan" | "purple" | "solar"` is written out twice (line 70 useState,
  line 113 localStorage.getItem cast). Drift hazard: if a new theme is
  added, both must be updated. Should be a shared `type ThemeName`
  exported from a constants file.

■ FEAT-12-E | LOW | Type mismatch: TUTORIALS shape vs DB TutorialItem
  Files: src/app/page.tsx:38-52 (local TutorialItem type, flat fields),
         src/app/page.tsx:66 (useState<typeof TUTORIALS[number]>),
         src/lib/content.ts:221-236 (TUTORIALS uses nested {en,de,fa})
  Issue: Two competing tutorial shapes exist:
    - content.ts TUTORIALS: `{ title: {en,de,fa}, level: {en,de,fa},
      description: {en,de,fa}, embedUrl, ... }`
    - page.tsx local TutorialItem (lines 38-52): `{ titleEn, titleFa,
      titleDe, levelEn, levelFa, levelDe, descEn, descFa, descDe,
      embedUrl, ... }` (flat, DB-shape)
  The local TutorialItem type is declared but NEVER USED (dead code).
  activeTutorial is typed as `typeof TUTORIALS[number]` (line 66), so
  `activeTutorial.title[lang]` (line 845) works for fallback content.
  But if ArchiveGrid passes DB-shaped tutorials (flat fields), the cast
  `as any` at line 685 hides the mismatch and `title[lang]` returns
  undefined → modal renders "undefined · {duration} · undefined".
  Fix: unify the type; delete the unused local TutorialItem.

■ FEAT-12-F | LOW | reCAPTCHA silent failure on missing env var
  Files: src/app/page.tsx:793, 345-351
  Issue: `data-sitekey={process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITEKEY || ""}`
  — if the env var is unset, sitekey is empty string. reCAPTCHA renders
  an error widget; `grecaptcha.getResponse()` returns "" (line 346);
  handleSubmit blocks submit with the hardcoded error message (line 348).
  User cannot submit the form at all, with no indication that the
  sitekey is misconfigured. Should detect empty sitekey and either
  skip reCAPTCHA (dev mode) or show a clear configuration error.

■ FEAT-12-G | LOW | http: protocol allowed in iframe src
  Files: src/app/page.tsx:859
  Issue: `if ((u.protocol === "https:" || u.protocol === "http:") && ...)`
  allows http:// embed URLs. CSP frame-src (per worklog SEC-08:122)
  lists only https:// hosts, so http:// would be blocked at runtime —
  defense-in-depth holds. But the page.tsx check is looser than CSP;
  a misconfigured DB row with http://aparat.com/... would render an
  empty iframe (CSP-blocked) with no user-visible error. Should
  restrict to https: only.

■ FEAT-12-H | LOW | Brand link has no aria-label
  Files: src/app/page.tsx:466
  Issue: `<a href="#hero" className="brand">` — relies on text content
  (brand-name span) for accessible name. Works, but if brand-name is
  empty (DB returns empty handle), the link has no accessible name.
  Edge case; minor.

================================================================================
CRITERION 1 — Expensive sync operations (bcrypt in hot path)?
================================================================================
VERDICT: NO sync bcrypt; ONE async-but-CPU-bound concern. LOW severity.

  PASS items:
  - src/lib/access-auth.ts:15  `import bcrypt from "bcryptjs"` — uses the
    pure-JS `bcryptjs` package, but every call is async/Promise-based:
      * hashPassword   (access-auth.ts:50-53)  → `await bcrypt.genSalt(10)`
                                                + `bcrypt.hash(...)`
      * verifyPassword (access-auth.ts:58-60)  → `bcrypt.compare(...)`
    No `bcrypt.compareSync` / `bcrypt.hashSync` anywhere in src/ (grep
    returned 0 hits).
  - Hot path (login) calls `verifyPassword` only ONCE per request:
      src/app/api/user/login/route.ts:66 `await verifyPassword(password,
      user.passwordHash)`. Correctly awaited, not Promise.all'd with DB.

  Concern (LOW):
  - `bcryptjs` (pure JS, package.json:17) is ~3-4× slower than the
    native `bcrypt` C++ binding. Even though the calls are async, the
    CPU work (~80-120 ms per compare at saltRounds=10) runs on the
    Node.js event-loop worker, not a thread pool. Under concurrent
    logins this can starve other in-flight requests. For a single-user
    portfolio this is fine; for a multi-access-user deployment it would
    matter. Mitigation: switch to `bcrypt` (native) OR add a worker.
  - `access-auth.ts:51` saltRounds=10 — reasonable default.

================================================================================
CRITERION 2 — Unnecessary DB queries?
================================================================================
VERDICT: YES — 4 instances. MEDIUM severity.

  Finding 2-A (MEDIUM): /api/chat POST runs `seedDefaultProviders()` on
  EVERY chat message.
    src/app/api/chat/route.ts:165-168
        const { callLLMWithFallback } = await import("@/lib/providers");
        const { seedDefaultProviders } = await import("@/lib/providers");
        await seedDefaultProviders();
    `seedDefaultProviders()` (src/lib/providers.ts:202-249) issues
    `db.aiProvider.count()` on every chat request even though seeding
    only ever runs once (it short-circuits when count>0). That is one
    extra round-trip per chat message for zero benefit after first run.
    Also: the same module is dynamically `import()`-ed twice on lines
    165 and 167 — should be a single destructure.
    Same issue duplicated in /api/admin/providers GET (line 20) — but
    that is admin-only, lower impact.

  Finding 2-B (MEDIUM): /api/chat POST reads kill-switch setting via
  `isApiEnabled()` on every chat message.
    src/app/api/chat/route.ts:100-101
        const { isApiEnabled } = await import("@/lib/settings");
        const apiEnabled = await isApiEnabled();
    `isApiEnabled()` (src/lib/settings.ts:44-47) does
    `db.siteSetting.findUnique({where:{key:"apiEnabled"}})` — one DB
    round-trip per chat message for a flag that changes ~once/month.
    No caching layer; would benefit from a 30-60s in-memory cache.

  Finding 2-C (LOW): /api/user/verify fetches the same AccessUser row
  twice in one request.
    src/app/api/user/verify/route.ts:22-27
        const user = await db.accessUser.findUnique({ where: { id: session.userId } });
        ...
        const access = await checkAccess(user.id);
    `checkAccess()` (src/lib/access-auth.ts:111-150) immediately does
    `db.accessUser.findUnique({ where: { id: userId } })` again —
    re-fetching the exact row already in `user`. Should pass `user`
    into `checkAccess` to avoid the duplicate query. Fires on every
    dashboard load + every time middleware lets a protected route
    through.

  Finding 2-D (LOW): /api/track writes one PageView row on every page
  visit (including every client-side re-mount after language change
  if `useContent` is re-instantiated).
    src/app/api/track/route.ts:20-28
    Hot path; SQLite handles it, but no batching, no sampling, no
    unique-by-(ip+path+minute) dedup. PageView table grows unbounded;
    admin/stats `count()` queries (admin/stats/route.ts:17-28) will
    slow as the table grows. Indexes exist (schema.prisma:172-173)
    so current impact is low.

  Finding 2-E (LOW): /api/contact POST calls `logSecurityEvent` 5× on
  the various error branches (lines 72, 79, 88, 107, 110), each an
  `await` on a `db.securityLog.create`. These block the 4xx response
  to the bot/spammer by ~5-20 ms each. Could be fire-and-forget
  (drop the `await`).

  Finding 2-F (LOW): /api/admin/content POST `toggle` action uses
  findUnique + update (2 queries) instead of a single conditional
  update.
    src/app/api/admin/content/route.ts:110-113
    Same pattern in admin/equipment/route.ts:78-83, admin/themes/
    route.ts:93-99, admin/nav/route.ts:58-61, admin/providers/route.ts:111-119.
    Could be replaced with a single `update` that flips the boolean

================================================================================
CRITERION 3 — N+1 query patterns?
================================================================================
VERDICT: YES — 2 instances. MEDIUM severity.

  Finding 3-A (MEDIUM): /api/admin/content GET — sequential await in a
  for-loop over 5 models.
    src/app/api/admin/content/route.ts:31-43
        for (const [name, model] of Object.entries(models)) {
          results[name + "s"] = await model.findMany({ orderBy: { order: "asc" } });
          ...
        }
    This issues 5 `findMany` calls SERIALLY even though they are
    independent. Total latency = sum of all 5 round-trips. Should be
    `Promise.all([...])` (compare with /api/content/route.ts:11-21
    which correctly uses Promise.all for the public endpoint).

  Finding 3-B (MEDIUM): /api/admin/content POST `bulk_import` —
  sequential `model.create` inside a for-loop.
    src/app/api/admin/content/route.ts:117-135
        for (const item of items) {
          try { ... await model.create({ data }); created++; } catch {}
        }
    Classic N+1 insert pattern. For N items, N sequential INSERTs.
    Prisma supports `db.<model>.createMany({ data: items })` in a
    single round-trip (with `skipDuplicates: true` to preserve the
    try/catch semantics). Same anti-pattern in:
    /api/admin/text POST `bulk_set` (src/app/api/admin/text/route.ts:74-95)
    — sequential `upsert` in a loop.

  Finding 3-C (LOW): /api/admin/clear POST `chat_all` / `message_all`
  issues 4 sequential `deleteMany` calls (lines 35-36, 52-55) where a
  single transaction or Prisma cascade delete could suffice. Acceptable
  for an admin "nuke" button.

  NON-N+1 (correctly batched, for the record):
  - /api/admin/stats/route.ts:16-28 — 11 queries via Promise.all ✓
  - /api/admin/security-dashboard/route.ts:20-27 — 6 queries via Promise.all ✓
  - /api/messages/route.ts:19-32 — findMany with `include: {replies,
    notes, tags:{include:{tag:true}}}` — properly eager-loaded, NOT N+1 ✓
  - /api/admin/users/logs/route.ts:33-43 — findMany with `include:{user:...}`
    + separate `count({where})` — 2 queries, correct ✓

CRITERION 4 — Are images optimized?
================================================================================
VERDICT: NO — Next/Image is not used anywhere. MEDIUM severity.

  Finding 4-A (MEDIUM): zero usage of `next/image` in the entire
  src/ tree (grep returned 0 hits for `next/image` or `Image from`).
  All imagery is served as raw `<img>` or via `next/font` CSS:
    - src/app/layout.tsx:48-54,61 — OG/Twitter image = `/icon-512.png`
      (a 512×512 PNG, presumably not WebP/AVIF).
    - src/app/layout.tsx:67-71 — favicon/icons `/icon-192.png`,
      `/icon-512.png` (PNG, not optimised for size/format negotiation).
    - public/icon-512.png, public/icon-192.png — only PNG variants
      shipped; no WebP/AVIF fallback.
  Impact: no lazy-loading, no responsive `srcset`, no automatic
  format negotiation, no blur placeholder. For a portfolio with
  mostly CSS/SVG decoration this is low impact, but every icon
  fetch is a separate unoptimised request.

  Finding 4-B (LOW): book covers are CSS gradients, not images
    (schema.prisma:203 `cover String @default("linear-gradient(...)")`).
    No image bytes shipped — GOOD for performance, but means the
    `next/image` opportunity is small.

    clips (page.tsx:707-729) use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to inject

    No `loading="lazy"` attribute added by `sanitizeEmbed.ts:41` —
    every iframe loads eagerly. Should add `loading="lazy"` to the

CRITERION 5 — Are there large client bundles?
================================================================================
VERDICT: YES — 3 issues. HIGH severity.

  Finding 5-A (HIGH): src/app/page.tsx (the visitor landing page) is
  "use client" (line 1) and statically imports FIVE admin-only
  components that are NEVER rendered in page.tsx:
    src/app/page.tsx:12   `import ContentManager from "@/components/ContentManager"`
    src/app/page.tsx:15   `import ThemeBuilder from "@/components/ThemeBuilder"`
    src/app/page.tsx:16   `import TextEditor from "@/components/TextEditor"`

    src/app/page.tsx:18   `import AccessUserManager from "@/components/AccessUserManager"`

  returned ZERO matches — these imports are dead. Each component
  pulls in its own state, fetch logic, and child components (e.g.
  AccessUserManager.tsx is ~330 lines, SettingsPanel is 967 lines).
  Result: every visitor's browser downloads, parses, and compiles
  ~5 admin components they will never see. Bundle could be reduced
  significantly by removing these 5 imports OR moving them to
  /user-dashboard (which already imports them at
  user-dashboard/page.tsx:14-21).

  TextEditor, NavMenuManager, ThemeBuilder, AccessUserManager,
  FontSelector, AparatClipManager, SettingsPanel). Even though only
  one tab is visible at a time, the entire dashboard ships in one
  chunk. Acceptable for admin-only page, but could be code-split
  with `next/dynamic` keyed on `activeTab`.

  Finding 5-C (LOW): page.tsx loads the reCAPTCHA script
  (https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js) on EVERY visitor mount
  regardless of whether they ever scroll to the contact form.
    src/app/page.tsx:82-89
    Should be deferred until the contact form is scrolled into view

CRITERION 7 — Are fonts loaded efficiently?
================================================================================
VERDICT: NO — 6 Google fonts loaded eagerly at root layout. MEDIUM.

  Finding 7-A (MEDIUM): src/app/layout.tsx:2,4 imports SIX Google
  fonts via `next/font/google`:
    layout.tsx:9   Geist            ({subsets:["latin"]})              — no display
    layout.tsx:10  Geist_Mono       ({subsets:["latin"]})              — no display
    layout.tsx:11  Vazirmatn        ({subsets:["arabic","latin"], display:"swap"})
    layout.tsx:17  Inter            ({subsets:["latin"]})              — no display
    layout.tsx:18  Lora             ({subsets:["latin"]})              — no display
    layout.tsx:19  Fira_Code        ({subsets:["latin"]})              — no display
  All six are loaded eagerly at the ROOT layout (applies to every
  page). Only ONE font is active at any time, controlled by
  `data-font` attribute (page.tsx:119 / SettingsPanel.tsx:296 /
  FontSelector.tsx:31). The other 5 are pure dead weight:
  - Vazirmatn pulls arabic+latin subsets (large).
  - Geist, Geist_Mono, Inter, Lora, Fira_Code each ship multiple
    weights (regular + bold at minimum).
  `next/font` self-hosts them (so no third-party request to
  fonts.googleapis.com — GOOD), but the woff2 bytes are still
  downloaded by every visitor. Recommendation: load only Vazirmatn
  (default) eagerly; lazy-load the others on first font-switch.

  Finding 7-B (MEDIUM): FIVE of the six fonts (lines 9,10,17,18,19)
  do NOT set `display: "swap"`. Only `vazirmatn` does (line 14).
  Missing `display:"swap"` causes FOIT (Flash of Invisible Text)
  for Geist/Geist_Mono/Inter/Lora/Fira_Code on first paint —
  visible delay before text renders, plus LCP regression.

  Finding 7-C (LOW): layout.tsx:113-125 injects an inline script
  into `<head>` to read `localStorage.site_font` and set the
  `data-font` attribute BEFORE hydration (good — prevents FOUC).
  This pattern is correct; no change needed.

  Finding 7-D (LOW): FontSelector.tsx lists 5 font choices
  (FontSelector.tsx:12-18): vazirmatn, inter, lora, fira-code,
  geist-mono. Matches the 5 switchable fonts in layout.tsx. Good —
  no orphan fonts.

CRITERION 9 — Are there blocking scripts?
================================================================================
VERDICT: PARTIAL — one blocking script injection. LOW-MEDIUM.

  Finding 9-A (LOW-MEDIUM): src/app/page.tsx:82-89 dynamically
  injects the reCAPTCHA script into `<head>` on mount:
      const s = document.createElement("script");
      s.src = "https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api.js";
      s.async = true; s.defer = true;
      document.head.appendChild(s);
  `async` + `defer` are correctly set (so it does not block
  parsing), BUT the script is appended on EVERY page mount
  regardless of whether the visitor ever reaches the contact form.
  reCAPTCHA api.js pulls ~1 KB of bootstrap + an iframe + ~50 KB
  of additional JS on execution. Should be deferred until the
  contact form is visible (IntersectionObserver pattern already
  used elsewhere in the same file at line 267).

  Finding 9-B (LOW): src/app/layout.tsx:113-125 — inline `<script>`
  in `<head>` that reads `localStorage.site_font` and sets
  `data-font` on `<html>` before hydration. This IS render-blocking
  (synchronous inline script in <head>), but it is <100 bytes and
  REQUIRED to prevent FOUC of the wrong font. Acceptable trade-off.

  Finding 9-C (LOW): src/app/layout.tsx:127-142 — inline JSON-LD
    `<script type="application/ld+json">` in `<head>`. Not
    render-blocking (browser skips `application/ld+json` for
    execution). Fine.

  Finding 9-D (LOW): per-frame `import("@/lib/canvas-protect")` calls
    inside canvas draw loops — see CRITERION 11 (memory leaks) for
    details; this is more of a CPU than a network concern because
    the module is cached after first load.

================================================================================
CRITERION 11 — Are there memory leaks?
================================================================================
VERDICT: PARTIAL — 3 leak risks + 2 per-frame anti-patterns. MEDIUM.

  Finding 11-A (MEDIUM): dynamic `import("@/lib/canvas-protect")`
  called INSIDE the `requestAnimationFrame` draw loop, on EVERY
  frame (~60 fps):
    src/components/RealOscilloscope.tsx:376-378
    src/components/LabDeviceVisualizer.tsx:402-404
    src/components/RealSignalGenerator.tsx:225-227
  Code:
      import("@/lib/canvas-protect").then(({ watermarkCanvas }) => {
        watermarkCanvas(ctx, w, h);
      });
  Although ES module imports are cached after first resolution, each
  call still:
    1. Allocates a new Promise,
    2. Schedules a microtask to look up the module record,
    3. Allocates a new closure for the `.then()` callback,
    4. Calls `watermarkCanvas` AFTER the frame has already been
       committed (because the import is async) — so the watermark
       for frame N is drawn on top of frame N+1.
  At 60 fps this is 60 Promise allocations + 60 microtask
  scheduling per canvas per second. Three components do this
  simultaneously on the about/signal-lab sections.
  Fix: hoist to module scope (`import { watermarkCanvas } from
  "@/lib/canvas-protect"`) and call directly.

  Finding 11-B (MEDIUM): `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)`
  called 5-8 times per frame inside the same draw loops:
    RealOscilloscope.tsx:141-147  (7 reads)
    LabDeviceVisualizer.tsx:57-64 (8 reads)
    RealSignalGenerator.tsx:123-128 (5 reads)
  `getComputedStyle` forces a style recalc on the document element.
  Called at 60 fps × 7-8 calls = 360-480 forced style recalcs/sec
  per canvas. Should cache once on mount + re-read only when
  `data-theme` attribute changes (MutationObserver on `<html>`).

  Finding 11-C (LOW): src/middleware.ts:58-64 — module-scope
  `setInterval` that GCs the rateLimitMap every 5 minutes:
      if (typeof setInterval !== "undefined") {
        setInterval(() => { ... }, 5 * 60 * 1000).unref?.();
      }
  The `.unref?.()` correctly prevents the interval from keeping
  the process alive. In Edge Runtime this branch is skipped
  (`setInterval` undefined). In Node runtime, ONE interval per
  process — fine. NOT a leak. Note: rateLimitMap itself is bounded
  by unique IPs × paths and GC'd, so no unbounded growth.

  Finding 11-D (LOW): src/app/api/chat/route.ts:9 and
  src/app/api/contact/route.ts:8 — in-memory `hits: Map<string,
  number[]>` rate limiters. Maps grow with unique IPs but each
  entry is GC'd when its timestamps expire (filter on each access).
  However there is NO periodic sweep — old IPs that never make a
  second request stay in the Map forever (their `arr` shrinks to
  [] but the key is never deleted). Long-running process → slow
  growth. Same pattern in src/app/api/user/login/route.ts:22
  (`loginAttempts: Map`) and middleware.ts:42 (`rateLimitMap`, but
  that one IS swept by 11-C).

  Finding 11-E (LOW): src/components/ChatSection.tsx:55-78 —
  `lastPollTs` is in the `useEffect` dep array AND updated inside
  the polling callback (lines 73, 108). Every time a poll returns
  new messages, `setLastPollTs` changes state → effect re-runs →
  old interval is cleared + new interval started. Not a leak
  (cleanup runs), but causes interval churn: each new message
  resets the 3-second polling cadence. Also: if `sessionId`
  changes, the old fetch can still resolve and call setState on
  the (now-stale) closure — no AbortController.

  Finding 11-F (LOW): src/app/page.tsx:91-98 — `fetch("/api/clips")`
  with no AbortController. If the component unmounts mid-fetch
  (route change), the `.then()` will call `setAparatClips` on an
  unmounted component. React 19 silently ignores this, but it is
  still a code smell. Same pattern in:
    useContent.ts:42-66 (has `cancelled` flag — GOOD),
    StatsDashboard.tsx:8-16 (no abort),
    SecurityDashboard.tsx:8-16 (no abort),
    TextEditor.tsx:14-22 (no abort),
    ContentManager.tsx:26-55 (no abort),
    AparatClipManager.tsx:35-55 (no abort).

  Finding 11-G (LOW): src/lib/db.ts:8-20 — global Prisma client
  singleton via `globalThis.prisma`. In dev (`NODE_ENV !== "production"`)
  the client is cached on globalThis to survive HMR; in production a
  new client is created per cold start. Correct pattern. No leak.

  - src/components/SignalBars.tsx:12-18        — returns at 17 (clearInterval).
  - src/components/ChatSection.tsx:58-78       — returns at 77 (clearInterval).
  - src/components/InteractiveTerminal.tsx:18,23 — no listeners/timers, no cleanup needed.
  - src/lib/useContent.ts:33-69                — returns at 68 (sets `cancelled` flag).

  MISSING / INCOMPLETE cleanups:

  Finding 12-A (LOW): src/app/page.tsx:79-99 — mount effect that
  injects the reCAPTCHA script and fetches `/api/clips`. Returns
  NO cleanup. The injected `<script id="recaptcha-api-script">`
  tag persists after unmount (acceptable — it is idempotent on
  re-mount via the `getElementById` guard), but the in-flight
  `fetch("/api/clips")` is not abortable. If the user navigates
  away before the fetch resolves, `setAparatClips` fires on an
  unmounted component. Fix: add `AbortController` and return
  `() => controller.abort()`.

  Finding 12-B (LOW): src/components/TextEditor.tsx:46,
  src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:358, src/components/PgpKey.tsx:18 —
  `setTimeout(() => setState(...), 2000-3000)` with no cleanup.
  If the component unmounts before the timeout fires, React 19
  will warn (or silently drop) the setState on unmounted
  component. Fix: store the timeout id in a ref and clear it in
  the effect cleanup, OR move the timeout into a useEffect.

  Finding 12-C (LOW): src/components/StatsDashboard.tsx:23,
  src/components/SecurityDashboard.tsx:23, src/components/
  AparatClipManager.tsx:35, src/components/ContentManager.tsx:60,
  src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:28, src/components/
  ThemeBuilder.tsx:78, src/components/TextEditor.tsx:29,
  src/components/AccessUserManager.tsx:80 — `useEffect(() => {
  load(); }, [])` patterns where `load` is a function defined in
  the component body (not memoised). ESLint
  `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` would warn. Not a leak per se,
  but the empty-deps array means `load` is captured stale — if
  `load` references state that changes, the closure will use the
  initial value. In all listed cases `load` only uses `setX`
  setters (stable), so behaviour is correct, but lint is unhappy.

  Finding 12-D (LOW): src/components/LabDeviceVisualizer.tsx:30-416
  effect depends on `[active, category, specs]` (line 416). The
  `specs` prop is declared in the deps array but never READ inside
  the effect body — it is only used in the JSX below. This is
  harmless (no extra cleanup), but the dep is misleading. Remove
  `specs` from the deps array OR add a comment explaining.

  also serializes 4 DB writes (findUnique session → create user msg

  the last two could be parallelised.

    `.dashboard-shell` → `.dashboard-container`. CSS at personal.css:3089-3117

    at <=768px. So the OUTER shell is mobile-aware.

    `overflow-x: auto; flex-wrap: nowrap` ✓ — horizontally scrollable. PASS.

    queries. Specifically:
      * ContentManager.tsx:193 uses `display:flex, gap:8, flexWrap:wrap` for action

      column <140px, textareas usable but cramped. Borderline.
    * ThemeBuilder.tsx:139  2-col grid editor+preview — at <400px preview box
      may clip. Borderline.
    * NavMenuManager.tsx:119  5-button action row — no flex-wrap, at <360px
      buttons squish to unreadable. ❌ FEAT-13-X5
    * reCAPTCHA iframe (page.tsx:792) — fixed 304px width from grecaptcha.js.
      On viewports <304px+padding, clipped. ❌ (same as FEAT-13-F1)
    * NavMenuManager.tsx:99  3-col grid for EN/FA/DE inputs — at <400px each
      col <120px. Borderline.
    * NavMenuManager.tsx:104  2-col grid link+select (2fr 1fr) — at <360px the
      select becomes <80px. Borderline.

  - Confirmed NOT overflowing (proper handling):
    * AccessUserManager.tsx:474  Users table — wrapped in `overflowX: "auto"` ✓
    * ArchiveGrid.tsx:85-116  `.archive-controls` — `flex-wrap: wrap` (CSS 2411) ✓
    * ArchiveGrid.tsx:197-248  `.archive-pagination` — `flex-wrap: wrap` (CSS 2434) ✓
    * ContentManager.tsx:193  action row — `flexWrap: "wrap"` ✓
    * AparatClipManager.tsx:366,388  day picker + permission buttons — `flexWrap: "wrap"` ✓

  - Potential overflow at extremely narrow widths (<280px):
    * `.skills-grid` minmax(260px, 1fr) — at <280px viewport single column would
      still be 260px wide, slightly overflowing. Body clip handles it.
    * `.books-grid` minmax(260px, 1fr) — same.
    * `.tutorials-grid` minmax(280px, 1fr) — same.
    * `.equipment-grid` minmax(220px, 1fr) — same.
    * `.osc-controls` minmax(160px, 1fr) — has mobile rule (<=720px → 1fr) ✓

■ Q6. Is the homepage responsive?
  Verdict: ✅ MOSTLY YES — primary breakpoints work; minor issues with nav-right
           density and `.article-row` on very narrow screens.

  Evidence (page.tsx + personal.css):
  - Hero section (page.tsx:542-566 + personal.css:463-509):
      * `.hero-grid` 1fr 1fr → 1fr at <=900px (CSS 1330) ✓
      * `.hero-visual` reorders above text at <=900px (CSS 1331) ✓
      * `.hero-title` uses `clamp(2.4rem, 6vw, 4.5rem)` (CSS 486) ✓ fluid
      * `.hero-subtitle` uses `clamp(0.9rem, 1.4vw, 1.05rem)` (CSS 497) ✓
      * `.hero-cta` switches to flex-column at <=480px (CSS 1376) ✓
      * `.btn` becomes full-width at <=480px (CSS 1377) ✓
    PASS.
  - About grid (page.tsx:584-615 + personal.css:634-720):
      * `.about-grid` 1.5fr 1fr → 1fr at <=900px (CSS 1332) ✓
      * `.about-card` position:static at <=900px (CSS 1333) ✓
      * `.about-stats` repeat(2,1fr) → 1fr at <=720px (CSS 1371) ✓
    PASS.
  - Skills grid (page.tsx:623-636 + personal.css:723-774):
      * `.skills-grid` repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr)) ✓ fluid
      * At viewport <280px (very rare) single column would still be 260px → tiny
        overflow, body clip handles it.
    PASS.
  - Books grid (page.tsx + personal.css:776-866):
      * `.books-grid` repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr)) ✓
    PASS.
  - Articles list (page.tsx + personal.css:868-926):
      * `.article-row` grid auto 1fr auto → 1fr at <=900px (CSS 1335-1339) ✓
      * At <=480px no further rule; `.article-date` is `white-space: nowrap`
        (CSS 893) — long dates (e.g. "2025-01-15") fit in 320px ✓
    PASS.
  - Tutorials grid (page.tsx + personal.css:928-1020):
      * `.tutorials-grid` repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)) ✓
      * `.tutorial-filters` flex-wrap (CSS 1724) ✓
    PASS.
  - Clips section (page.tsx:694-733) — Aparat video clips:
      * Inline `<div style={{aspectRatio:"16/9"}}>` ✓ responsive via aspect-ratio
      * Title bar `<div style={{padding:"12px 16px"}}>` — no mobile rule but
        16px padding works on phones.
    PASS.
  - Contact section (page.tsx:735-806 + personal.css:1082-1179):
      * `.contact-grid` 1fr 1.2fr → 1fr at <=900px (CSS 1334) ✓
      * `.contact-form` padding 24px — no mobile rule. At <480px the form is
        24px-padded inside a 16px-padded container → ~256px usable. Tight.
        ⚠️ FEAT-13-H8
      * reCAPTCHA iframe width 304px — overflow issue (FEAT-13-F1) ❌
    PARTIAL.
  - Footer (page.tsx:810-828 + personal.css:1181-1216):
      * `.footer-inner` flex → column at <=720px (CSS 1372) ✓
    PASS.
  - Navbar (page.tsx:464-541 + personal.css:348-460):
      * `.nav-links` becomes a fixed drawer at <=720px (CSS 1347-1364) ✓
      * `.nav-toggle` (hamburger) shown at <=720px (CSS 1370) ✓
      * RTL drawer flips side at <=720px (CSS 1399-1406) ✓
      * BUT `.nav-right` (page.tsx:508) contains `.theme-switcher` (7 buttons
        at CSS 2051, padding 5px 8px each ~15px wide + 10px theme-icon = ~25px
        each = ~175px total) + `.lang-toggle` (3 buttons, ~70px) + `.nav-toggle`
        hamburger (~30px). Total ~275px. On a 360px viewport with `.brand` on
        the left (~80px) and gap 16px, nav-right has only ~265px available.
        Theme-switcher may clip or push brand off-canvas. Body overflow-x:
        hidden masks it but theme buttons at the right edge become inaccessible.
        ❌ FEAT-13-H9
      * On a 320px viewport (iPhone SE), 7 theme buttons + 3 lang buttons + 1
        hamburger + brand = definitely overflows.
    PARTIAL.

■ Q7. Are iframes responsive?
  Verdict: ✅ YES — all iframes use 100% width with aspect-ratio or absolute
           fill.

  Evidence:
  - Tutorial modal iframe (page.tsx:851-871):
      * Wrapper `.tutorial-modal-video` (personal.css:1068-1080):
        `position: relative; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; background: #000;`
      * iframe (CSS 1074-1080): `position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%;
        height: 100%; border: 0;`
      PASS — proper aspect-ratio responsive iframe.
  - Aparat clip embeds (page.tsx:724-727):
      * Wrapper `<div style={{aspectRatio: "16/9", background: "#000"}}>` with
        `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` from `sanitizeEmbed(clip.embedCode)`.
      * sanitize-embed.ts enforces Aparat/YouTube/Vimeo allow-list (per prior
        SEC-08 audit). The injected iframe inherits 100% width from Aparat's
        embed code (Aparat's standard embed uses `style="width:100%;..."`).
      PASS — responsive via aspect-ratio wrapper.
  - reCAPTCHA iframe (page.tsx:792-795):
      * Container `<div className="g-recaptcha">` has no explicit width.
      * grecaptcha.js injects an iframe with a fixed `width="304"` attribute.
      * At viewport <304px + form padding, this iframe overflows the form.
      * Body `overflow-x: hidden` clips it silently.
      ⚠️ PARTIAL — Google's iframe is the issue, not our CSS. The clip means
      users on <320px viewports cannot complete the captcha (cannot scroll to
      see all of it). Consider `transform: scale(0.9)` or `data-size="compact"`
      (reCAPTCHA v2 compact size).
      ❌ FEAT-13-I1

■ Q8. Are modals full-screen on mobile?
  Verdict: ❌ NO — neither admin nor tutorial modal has a mobile full-screen
           variant. Both have max-width constraints + max-height that leave
           them constrained in the center of the screen.

  Evidence:
  - `.admin-modal` (personal.css:1251-1261):
      `position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.95); z-index: 2000;
       display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 20px;`
      → Modal is centered with 20px padding around it. On a 360px viewport,
        modal width is ~320px max (360 - 2×20 padding).
    `.admin-modal-inner` (CSS 1262-1271):
      `max-width: 700px; width: 100%; max-height: 85vh; display: flex;
       flex-direction: column;`
      → At 360px viewport, modal is 320px wide × 85vh tall, centered.
      → No @media rule switches this to `inset: 0; max-width: none;
        max-height: 100vh; border-radius: 0` on mobile.
    ❌ FEAT-13-M1
  - `.tutorial-modal` (personal.css:1023-1043):
      Same pattern: `padding: 20px;` around `.tutorial-modal-inner` with
      `max-width: 900px; max-height: 90vh`.
      On mobile the modal is constrained to (viewport - 40px) wide × 90vh tall.
      Video is 16:9 aspect ratio inside.
      ❌ FEAT-13-M2
  - `.anti-theft-warning` (personal.css:2255-2271) — IS full-screen via
      `inset: 0; padding: 40px;` and `.anti-theft-warning-content { max-width:
      500px; }`. But this is a warning overlay, not a user-interactive modal.
    PASS for its use case.
  - `.global-search-overlay` / `.global-search-modal` — referenced in
    GlobalSearch.tsx:87-88 but the CSS classes ARE NOT DEFINED anywhere in
    personal.css or globals.css (Grep returned 0 matches). GlobalSearch.tsx
    is also never imported by any other file (Grep returned only the
    component's own definition). DEAD component. Not a runtime concern but
    a maintenance hazard.
    ⚠️ FEAT-13-M3 (dead component, dead CSS class refs)

  Mobile modal best practice is to make modals full-screen at <=600px or
  <=480px (e.g., `position: fixed; inset: 0; max-width: 100%; max-height: 100%;
  border-radius: 0; padding: 16px;`). Neither admin nor tutorial modal does
  this.

■ Q9. Is the chat usable on mobile?
  Verdict: ⚠️ PARTIAL — chat is readable but input touch target is small and
           no mobile-specific layout rule exists.

  Evidence (ChatSection.tsx + personal.css:1494-1637):
  - `.chat-window` (CSS 1494-1502): `max-width: 700px; margin: 0 auto;`
      → on mobile correctly constrained to viewport width ✓
  - `.chat-bar` (CSS 1503-1513): `display: flex; justify-content: space-between;
      align-items: center; padding: 8px 14px; font-size: 0.72rem;`
      → 3 children (callsign, bar-title "encrypted · simplex", bar-meta "N msg")
        at narrow widths squish but don't overflow. The "encrypted · simplex"
        label (CSS 1530) at 0.72rem is likely first to clip. Borderline.
      ⚠️ FEAT-13-C1
  - `.chat-body` (CSS 1533-1545): `padding: 18px; min-height: 320px; max-height:
      440px; overflow-y: auto;`
      → On mobile this is a 320-44px wide × 320-440px tall scrollable area ✓
  - `.chat-msg` (CSS 1547-1551): `max-width: 85%;`
      → at narrow widths 85% of (viewport - 36px padding) leaves 15% gap ✓
      → No mobile rule reduces max-width to 92% or 95% on phones. Acceptable.
  - `.chat-input-row` (CSS 1608-1615): `display: flex; align-items: center;
      gap: 8px; padding: 12px 14px;`
      → 3 children: prompt "tx>" + input + submit button. At narrow widths the
        submit button (ChatSection.tsx:190-192 uses `.btn btn-primary btn-sm`
        → CSS 297 padding 6px 12px → ~28px tall + "tx [enter]" text wraps to
        ~2 lines on very narrow screens). Input gets the remaining width.
      → Submit button touch target ~28px ❌ FEAT-13-C2
  - `.chat-input` (CSS 1622-1632): `padding: 8px 10px; font-size: 0.85rem;`
      → Touch target ~32px tall ❌ FEAT-13-C3
  - `.chat-prompt` (CSS 1616-1621): `font-size: 0.82rem; white-space: nowrap;`
      → "tx>" prefix on its own line — fine.
  - No mobile rule reduces `.chat-body` max-height or expands `.chat-input-row`
    padding on mobile.
  - Submit button label "tx [enter]" (ChatSection.tsx:132-134) at font-size
    0.78rem (CSS btn-sm) — wraps on narrow widths.

  Verdict: chat IS usable but tap targets and submit button label wrapping
  are friction points.

■ Q10. Is the contact form usable on mobile?
  Verdict: ⚠️ PARTIAL — form is functional, but inputs are <44px touch targets
           and reCAPTCHA iframe overflows on narrow viewports.

  Evidence (page.tsx:762-804 + personal.css:1082-1179):
  - Form layout: `.contact-grid` 1fr 1.2fr → 1fr at <=900px (CSS 1334) ✓
      Form takes full column width on mobile ✓
  - Form padding: `.contact-form` padding 24px (CSS 1126) — no mobile rule.
      At <=480px viewport (320-16=304px parent), form inner width is
      304 - 48 = 256px. Inputs are full-width of that 256px. Tight but usable.
      ⚠️ FEAT-13-CF1 (suggest 16px padding at <=480px)
  - Inputs (CSS 1146-1157): `width: 100%; padding: 10px 12px; font-size:
      0.88rem;` → touch target ~36-40px tall. Below WCAG 44px but close.
      ⚠️ FEAT-13-CF2
  - Textarea (CSS 1146-1157 with `resize: vertical`): `rows={5}` from
      page.tsx:784 — gives ~5 lines of typing space. Acceptable.
  - Submit button (page.tsx:800): `.btn btn-primary btn-block` → CSS 258
      padding 10px 20px, full-width. Touch target ~36px tall. Below 44px.
      ⚠️ FEAT-13-CF3
  - reCAPTCHA (page.tsx:791-795): Google's iframe at 304px wide overflows
      on <320px viewports. Body clips. ❌ (FEAT-13-F1 / FEAT-13-I1)
      Suggest using `data-size="compact"` (reCAPTCHA v2 compact size 150×140)
      on mobile via JS detection, or replacing with invisible captcha.
  - Honeypot field (page.tsx:764-771): positioned `left: -9999px` ✓ hidden
      from users, accessible to bots. Works on mobile.
  - Time-trap field (page.tsx:773): `<input type="hidden" name="_t">` ✓ works.
  - Form status (page.tsx:803): `.form-status` (CSS 1168-1179) text-align:
      center, min-height 1.2em, font-size 0.8rem ✓ readable.

  Overall: form submissions work; tapping accuracy is the friction point.

================================================================================
ADDITIONAL FINDINGS (beyond the 10 audit questions)
================================================================================

■ A1. Dead CSS class `.content-manager-type-tabs` / `.content-manager-type-tab`
  File: src/app/personal.css:2490-2513
  Issue: Selector defined but Grep returned 0 matches in any .tsx file. The
    ContentManager component uses `.admin-tabs` / `.admin-tab` instead
    (ContentManager.tsx:184-189). Dead CSS — maintenance hazard.
  Recommendation: remove or wire it up.

■ A2. Dead component GlobalSearch.tsx + 7 undefined CSS classes
  File: src/components/GlobalSearch.tsx:87-121 (uses `global-search-overlay`,
    `global-search-modal`, `global-search-input`, `global-search-results`,
    `global-search-result`, `global-search-icon`, `global-search-title`,
    `global-search-desc`, `global-search-type`)
  Issue: GlobalSearch.tsx is never imported by any other file (Grep: only
    self-references). If ever rendered, the modal would have NO positioning,
    NO overlay, NO styling — would render as a plain inline div, breaking
    the page layout. Not a runtime concern today but a landmine.

■ A3. Fixed-height canvas containers in Signal Lab
  Files:
    - src/components/RealOscilloscope.tsx:400    `<div style={{height: 220}}>`
    - src/components/RealSignalGenerator.tsx:256 `<div style={{height: 100}}>`
    - src/components/LabDeviceVisualizer.tsx:437 `<canvas style={{height: 150}}>`
  Issue: Inline fixed pixel heights — no responsive rule. On a 320px-wide
    phone the 220px-tall oscilloscope canvas is fine, but on a 768px tablet
    in landscape it stays 220px tall (wasted vertical space). The canvas
    itself uses `width:100%, height:100%` + ResizeObserver ✓ so it scales
    to its parent. The issue is the PARENT has a fixed pixel height. Minor.

■ A4. `.signal-waveform-selector` 4-column grid has no mobile rule
  File: src/app/personal.css:2195-2199
  Code: `display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); gap: 4px;`
  Issue: 4 columns fixed. At <320px viewport each cell <70px. Buttons inside
    use `.signal-waveform-btn` (padding 6px 4px) — labels like "SINE" / "SQR"
    / "SAW" / "TRI" fit but barely. Not a horizontal overflow issue (cells
    shrink), but touch targets drop below 28px tall.

■ A5. Inline `style={{}}` blocks throughout admin components have no
     responsive overrides
  Files: nearly every component in src/components/
  Issue: ContentManager, NavMenuManager, StatsDashboard, SecurityDashboard,
    TextEditor, ThemeBuilder, AccessUserManager, AparatClipManager all use
    inline styles with fixed `gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr"` or `"1fr 1fr 1fr"`
    or `"repeat(4, 1fr)"` and no `@media` rules (inline styles cannot have
    media queries anyway). To make these responsive, the layouts need to
    either (a) switch to className-based styling with @media rules in
    personal.css, or (b) use a `useMediaQuery` hook in JS. Currently neither
    is done. Architectural.

■ A6. Nav drawer (`.nav-links.open`) at <=720px has no close button
  File: src/app/personal.css:1347-1370
  Issue: Drawer is `position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; width: 70%; max-width:
    280px;` and slides in via `transform: translateX(0)`. There is no × close
    button inside the drawer. To close, the user must tap the hamburger again
    (page.tsx:530-541 — `onClick={() => setMenuOpen(!menuOpen)}`) or tap a
    nav link (page.tsx:469 — `onClick={(e) => handleNavClick(e, "#hero")}`).
    On mobile this is workable but the lack of an explicit close affordance
    in the drawer is a UX gap. Also: tapping outside the drawer does NOT
    close it (no overlay behind the drawer).

■ A7. Body has `overflow-x: hidden` (personal.css:137) which masks horizontal
     overflow instead of fixing root cause
  Issue: Already noted as FEAT-13-X1. Re-listing here as architectural concern.
    Any future component that overflows will be silently clipped (content
    inaccessible) rather than producing a visible bug for developers to fix.
    Consider removing `overflow-x: hidden` once root causes are addressed.

■ A8. `.to-top` button is 36×36px (personal.css:1222)
  Issue: Below WCAG 44×44. The button is bottom-right FAB, so it's a frequent
    touch target on mobile. ❌ already listed in Q4 inventory.

■ A9. Settings Panel provider editor has 2-col rows that drop to 1-col only
     at <=600px (CSS 2819-2823)
  Files: src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:868, 889 (two `.settings-row` blocks
    inside `.settings-provider-editor`)
  Issue: At viewport widths 601-900px (e.g., landscape phones, small tablets),
    these stay 2-col which is fine. At <600px drop to 1-col ✓. The only gap
    is in the 320-600px range where the 2-col→1-col breakpoint (600px) leaves
    a wide range of "OK but cramped" widths. Acceptable.

■ A10. RTL handling exists for nav drawer (personal.css:1399-1406) but not
     for other components
  Files: SettingsPanel.tsx:566 uses `dir={panelLang === "fa" ? "rtl" : "ltr"}`
    ✓. AccessUserManager, NavMenuManager, TextEditor, ThemeBuilder do NOT set
    dir attribute on their root — they inherit from `document.documentElement`
    which user-dashboard/page.tsx:96,119 sets based on lang. So RTL does work
    for the dashboard page. But individual inline styles like
    `marginLeft: 8` (NavMenuManager.tsx:124) and `marginRight: 4`
    (AccessUserManager.tsx:519) are physical, not logical — they don't flip
    in RTL. Minor visual asymmetry.

  Recent activity row — `display:flex; gap:8` with fixed widths 140 + 100 +

  Headline issues:
  (1) Touch targets — 53 elements below WCAG 44px. Pervasive.
  (2) Horizontal overflow masked by `body { overflow-x: hidden }` — 5
      concrete overflow sites (H1-H7 cluster) need fixing at root.

  (5) Nav-right (theme-switcher 7 btns + lang-toggle 3 btns + hamburger)
      overflows on small phones; rightmost theme buttons inaccessible.
  (6) reCAPTCHA v2 standard size (304×78) overflows on <320px viewports.
  (7) Multiple admin sub-components use inline 2/3-col grids with no @media
      rules — they cannot be made responsive without refactoring to
      className-based CSS or adding a useMediaQuery hook.
  (8) Dead code: GlobalSearch.tsx (component never imported) + 7 referenced
      CSS classes that don't exist; `.content-manager-type-tabs` CSS block
      is dead.

  Recommend: FEAT-14 mobile-responsiveness sprint addressing items 1-4
  above (touch targets, horizontal overflow root causes, modal full-screen,
  tab horizontal scroll). Items 5-8 can be follow-up. Item 7 (inline-style
  refactor) is architectural and likely a separate FEAT ticket.

================================================================================
DETAILED ISSUES (file:line references)
================================================================================

■ I-1 (LOW) — TextEditor.tsx loadTexts network-error swallowed
  Files:
    src/components/TextEditor.tsx:14-22 (loadTexts)
  Problem: `catch {}` empty. If fetch fails (offline, 502, DNS), the
    user sees no error message; `loading` becomes false and the empty
    state (`No text found`) is shown — indistinguishable from "no data
    yet." Backend also returns `{ ok: false, texts: {} }` on its own
    catch, which the frontend silently treats as "no texts."
  Severity: LOW (silent failure on read).

■ I-2 (MED) — TextEditor.tsx saveText: no error feedback, no try/catch
  Files:
    src/components/TextEditor.tsx:31-48 (saveText)
  Problem:
    (a) No `try/catch` around the POST fetch. If the network fails, the
        promise rejects unhandled → console error, no UI feedback.
    (b) `if (data.ok)` only sets savedKey indicator. No `else` branch —
        if backend returns `{ ok: false, error: "unauthorized" }` or
        `{ ok: false, error: "missing_key" }`, the user gets no
        indication that the save failed. The ✓ "saved" toast never
        shows, but neither does any error.
  Backend returns (src/app/api/admin/text/route.ts:44, 48, 56, 99, 103):
    401 `{ ok: false, error: "unauthorized" }`
    400 `{ ok: false, error: "invalid_body" | "missing_key" | "invalid_action" }`
    500 `{ ok: false, error: "server_error" }`
  Severity: MED (user thinks text saved, but it isn't).

■ I-3 (LOW) — ThemeBuilder.tsx loadThemes empty catch + no error UI
  Files:
    src/components/ThemeBuilder.tsx:63-71
  Problem: `catch {}` empty. Same pattern as I-1 — network failure shows
    "No custom themes yet" misleadingly.
  Severity: LOW.

■ I-4 (MED) — ThemeBuilder.tsx saveTheme: error swallowed, no network catch path
  Files:
    src/components/ThemeBuilder.tsx:80-99 (saveTheme)
  Problem:
    (a) `try/catch` exists but catch body is empty (`catch {}`). If the
        POST request throws (network failure, JSON parse error on
        non-JSON 502 body), no UI feedback.
    (b) `if (data.ok) { setEditing(null); loadThemes(); }` has no else.
        On `{ ok: false, error: "unauthorized" | "missing_id" | "not_found"
        | "invalid_action" }`, the editor stays open with no error
        message — user may click "save" repeatedly, never realizing the
        server is rejecting.
  Severity: MED.

■ I-5 (MED) — ThemeBuilder.tsx deleteTheme & toggleTheme fire-and-forget
  Files:
    src/components/ThemeBuilder.tsx:101-109 (deleteTheme)
    src/components/ThemeBuilder.tsx:111-118 (toggleTheme)
  Problem:
    (a) `await fetch(...)` — no `const res =` / no `data.ok` check.
    (b) No try/catch — network failure throws unhandled.
    (c) `loadThemes()` is called unconditionally after, so the UI
        refreshes regardless of success/failure. If the delete failed
        (e.g., 401 unauthorized, or 500 server error), the theme
        still appears in the list — user thinks delete worked but it
        didn't.
  Severity: MED.

■ I-6 (LOW) — SettingsPanel.tsx loadSettings/loadProviders empty catch on load
  Files:
    src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:299-346 (loadSettings)
    src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:348-354 (loadProviders)
  Problem: Both functions have `try { ... } catch { /* ignore */ }`.
    Network failure silently leaves the form fields empty. The `finally`
    sets `loading=false` so the user sees an empty form with no error
    indication.
  Mitigation: `postJSON` helper at line 361-374 handles errors
    properly (returns `{ ok: false, error: "network" }`), so all
    *mutations* via postJSON show error toasts. Only the initial loads
    are silent.
  Severity: LOW.

■ I-7 (INFO) — SettingsPanel.tsx:305 calls /api/content with credentials
  Files:
    src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:305
    src/app/api/content/route.ts:9-58 (public, no auth check)
  Observation: This is a public endpoint (no checkAdminAuth), so
    credentials: 'include' is unnecessary but harmless. The endpoint
    returns ALL SiteSettings as a flat object — including potentially
    sensitive keys (baleBotToken, telegramBotToken, forwardEmail,
    handle) if they exist in the DB. This is a backend-side information
    disclosure issue (public endpoint exposing admin-set secrets), but
    the *contract* between SettingsPanel.tsx and /api/content is
    consistent: frontend reads `contentData.settings.name_fa` etc.
    which are present in the response.
  Severity: INFO (contract matches; backend over-shares — out of
    scope for this audit but flagged).

■ I-8 (LOW) — ContentManager.tsx loadItems: error sets `items=[]` (silent)
  Files:
    src/components/ContentManager.tsx:26-55 (loadItems)
  Problem: `catch { setItems([]); }` — network error or server error
    makes the list appear empty ("No items yet."). The `if (data.ok)`
    branch handles `{ ok: false, error: ... }` by setting items=[], so
    auth failure (401) looks identical to "no content created yet."
  Severity: LOW.

■ I-9 (MED) — ContentManager.tsx saveItem/deleteItem/toggleItem/bulkImport:
              fire-and-forget mutations, silent failures
  Files:
    src/components/ContentManager.tsx:62-81 (saveItem)
    src/components/ContentManager.tsx:83-92 (deleteItem)
    src/components/ContentManager.tsx:94-102 (toggleItem)
    src/components/ContentManager.tsx:104-120 (bulkImport)
  Problem (per mutation):
    saveItem: `await fetch(...)` — no `data.ok` check, no error UI.
      `catch {}` empty. Network failure → editor closes, list reloads
      silently. Item may or may not be saved.
    deleteItem: same — no `data.ok` check, no try/catch. Network
      failure throws unhandled promise rejection.
    toggleItem: same — fire-and-forget, then `loadItems()`.
    bulkImport: `if (data.ok) { alert(...); }` — no else branch. If
      backend returns `{ ok: false, error: "no_items" | "invalid_type"
      | "invalid_action" | "server_error" }`, the alert never fires,
      the bulkText is NOT cleared, the bulkImport modal stays open,
      and the user has no idea why nothing happened. They may paste
      the JSON again and click "import" repeatedly.
  Severity: MED (most damaging for bulkImport — user retries
    repeatedly thinking the import didn't fire).

■ I-10 (HIGH/CRITICAL) — ContentManager.tsx:109 bulk_import on EQUIPMENT
              endpoint — backend has no bulk_import case
  Files:
    src/components/ContentManager.tsx:108-113
    src/app/api/admin/equipment/route.ts:49-87 (switch has only
      create / update / delete / toggle — NO bulk_import)
  Reproduction:
    1. Open ContentManager with activeType="equipment".
    2. Paste `[{ "name": "Spec Analyzer", "model": "X" }]` into bulk
       import box, click "import."
    3. Frontend POSTs `{ type: "equipment", action: "bulk_import",
       items: [...] }` to `/api/admin/equipment`.
    4. Backend switch falls through to `default: return 400 { ok:
       false, error: "invalid_action" }` (route.ts:86-87).
    5. Frontend: `data.ok` is false → `if (data.ok)` branch is
       skipped. No `else`. No catch fires (res.json() succeeded).
       Nothing happens. Modal stays open, text unchanged, no error.
    6. User retries, possibly 10× — each time hits the same 400.
  Severity: HIGH (feature is silently broken for the equipment type;
    user has no feedback that it's broken).
  Note: This same issue is documented as "Q5-D1" in worklog.md FEAT-02
    audit (line 26060). Re-confirmed here. NOT FIXED.

■ I-11 (LOW) — AparatClipManager.tsx handleDelete silent on data.ok=false
  Files:
    src/components/AparatClipManager.tsx:88-101 (handleDelete)
  Problem: `await fetch(...)` (no `data.ok` check), then `fetchClips()`.
    Catch block does `alert("خطا در حذف")` only for thrown network
    errors. If backend returns `{ ok: false, error: "unauthorized" }`
    or 500, no alert — the clip appears to be deleted in UI (because
    fetchClips reloads), but actually wasn't.
  Severity: LOW.

■ I-12 (HIGH) — StatsDashboard.tsx:11 password in URL + missing
              credentials + empty catch
  Files:
    src/components/StatsDashboard.tsx:11
  Problems:
    (a) `fetch(\`/api/admin/stats?password=${password}\`)` — passes
        admin password in URL query string. Logged in nginx access
        logs, browser history, referrer headers, CDN logs.
        VIOLATION of audit criterion #9.
    (b) No `credentials: "include"` option. Session cookie is NOT
        sent (cross-origin) or may be omitted depending on browser
        default for fetch. Backend reads password from URL but
        ignores it (admin-auth.ts:17-18 — V17.2 removed password
        fallback). So this call authenticates via cookie ONLY —
        but the cookie isn't sent! → 401 unauthorized.
        VIOLATION of audit criterion #5.
    (c) `catch {}` empty. 401 → data.ok false → no UI error. Just
        shows "No data." (line 26). User has no idea they're not
        authenticated.
        VIOLATION of audit criterion #6 and #8.
  Component is ORPHAN (no importer found — confirmed via grep, see
    worklog.md:10809, 12412). Latent vuln reactivates if wired back.
  Severity: HIGH (latent, but 3 simultaneous violations).

■ I-13 (LOW) — NavMenuManager.tsx loadItems empty catch + no error UI
  Files:
    src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:13-21 (loadItems)
  Problem: `catch {}` empty. Network failure shows empty list with
    no error indication.
  Severity: LOW.

■ I-14 (MED) — NavMenuManager.tsx save/del/toggle/move: fire-and-forget,
              no error feedback, no try/catch
  Files:
    src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:30-44 (save)
    src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:46-54 (del)
    src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:56-63 (toggle)
    src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:65-81 (move)
  Problem: All four mutations follow the same anti-pattern:
    `await fetch(...); setEditing(null); loadItems();` — no `data.ok`
    check, no try/catch around fetch. If network fails or backend
    returns 401/400/500, the mutation appears to succeed in the UI
    (because loadItems is called regardless), but actually didn't.
  Severity: MED.

■ I-15 (LOW) — NavMenuManager.tsx move() non-atomic swap
  Files:
    src/components/NavMenuManager.tsx:65-81 (move)
  Problem: Move up/down does `Promise.all([update(a, b.order),
    update(b, a.order)])`. If only one fetch succeeds (network
    glitch, 500 on one), the two items end up with the SAME `order`
    value (both have b.order, or both have a.order). The next
    loadItems will show them in non-deterministic order. Also, the
    two POSTs are not wrapped in try/catch — if either rejects, the
    Promise.all rejects unhandled.
  Severity: LOW (rare race; visual glitch).

■ I-16 (LOW) — AccessUserManager.tsx fetchLogs no try/catch, no error UI
  Files:
    src/components/AccessUserManager.tsx:101-113 (fetchLogs)
  Problem: `try { ... } finally { ... }` — no catch. If fetch throws
    (network failure), the rejection bubbles to the click handler,

Backend password-ignoring confirmation:
  src/lib/admin-auth.ts:17-18 — checkAdminAuth(request, _password?):

    All admin routes read `String(body.password || "")` then pass to

SUMMARY

Audited 38 source files (layout, pages, components, lib). The codebase has

modal lacks `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`/focus-trap; iframe embeds lack
`title`; multiple themes fail color contrast on text-dim/text-faint tokens.

Compliance score (estimated): ~55% of WCAG 2.1 AA criteria pass.
Critical blockers: keyboard access (#1), labels (#3), landmarks (#10),
contrast (#6), color-only indicators (#7).

Q6 — Are there color contrast issues?
================================================================================
Computed contrast ratios against WCAG 2.1 AA thresholds (4.5:1 for normal
text, 3:1 for large text and UI components).

TERMINAL THEME (default — html[data-theme="terminal"] or no attribute):
  Defined in: src/app/personal.css:6-31

  FAIL — text-dim on backgrounds:
    - #4a7a4a on #000000 = 4.12:1 (FAIL 4.5:1)
    - #4a7a4a on #050d05 (--bg-panel) = ~4.06:1 (FAIL 4.5:1)
    - #4a7a4a on #030a03 (--bg-soft) = ~4.10:1 (FAIL 4.5:1)
    Used in: 49 selectors across personal.css (lines 248, 310, 342, 397, 428,
    524, 559, 679, 711, 755, 839, 898, 912, 1057, 1107, 1195, 1206, 1303,
    1511, 1652, 1671, 1692, 1729, 1848, 2029, 2054, 2120, 2159, 2203, 2359,
    2419, 2424, 2478, 2501, 2580, 2761, 2798, 2807, 2833, 2929, 2943, 3034,
    3056, 3141, 3240, 3288, 3314, 3375, 3402) — used for labels, hints,
    timestamps, secondary text, captions, .section-eyebrow etc.

  FAIL — text-faint on backgrounds:
    - #2a4a2a on #000000 = ~2.08:1 (FAIL 4.5:1)
    - #2a4a2a on #050d05 = ~2.05:1 (FAIL 4.5:1)
    Used in: 16 selectors across personal.css (lines 535, 739, 1160, 1213,
    1530, 1531, 1563, 1633 [placeholder], 1712, 1776, 2129, 2301 [placeholder],
    2861, 3047, 3381, 3438) — used for very dim hints, placeholders, metadata.

  BORDERLINE — green-dim on backgrounds:
    - #008f11 on #000000 = ~4.9:1 (PASS but borderline; fails at small sizes
      if used for body text). Used for .section-eyebrow, .btn::before,
      waveform labels. Mostly OK.

CLEAN THEME (light):
  Defined in: src/app/personal.css:23-39
  FAIL — text-faint #a0a0b0 on #f5f6f8 = ~2.35:1 (FAIL)
  FAIL — green-dim #4a8fde on #f5f6f8 = ~3.0:1 (FAIL for normal text)
  PASS — text-dim #6a6a7a on #f5f6f8 = ~4.7:1 (PASS)

MIDNIGHT THEME (dark blue):
  Defined in: src/app/personal.css:54-71
  FAIL — text-dim #6a7a9a on #0a0e1a = ~4.49:1 (borderline FAIL — at exactly
    4.5:1 threshold, fails at typical gamma)
  FAIL — text-faint #3a4a6a on #0a0e1a = ~2.24:1 (FAIL)
  FAIL — green-dim #2a6ec0 on #0a0e1a = ~3.93:1 (FAIL for normal text)

Also applies to inline styles that use var(--text-dim, #4a7a4a) with hardcoded
fallback — the fallback itself fails contrast.

WCAG: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (AA) — pervasive violation across all 3 themes.

Q1. Does matcher cover all /api/admin/* paths?

  ✅ YES — src/middleware.ts:220-228
  Code (lines 220-228):
    export const config = {
      matcher: [
        "/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\.(?:png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp|svg|ico|txt|xml|css|js|woff|woff2|ttf|eot)$).*)",
      ],

    /api/admin/settings, /api/admin/security, etc.) match the middleware
    because none of them start with _next/ or end in those extensions.
  Caveat (informational only):
    If a future file-serving route is added under /api/admin/* that ends
    in one of the excluded extensions (e.g. a hypothetical
    /api/admin/logs.js), it would be silently excluded from middleware.
    No such route exists today. Also note `.json` is NOT in the exclusion
    list, so JSON-returning API routes are correctly matched.

Q3. Is hasValidSession() secure? (HMAC verify or just format check?)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ❌ NO — src/middleware.ts:70-93  (HIGH)
  Code (lines 70-93):
    function hasValidSession(cookieHeader: string): boolean {
      if (!cookieHeader) return false;
      const cookies = Object.fromEntries(
        cookieHeader.split(";").map(c => {
          const [k, ...v] = c.trim().split("=");
          return [k, v.join("=")];
        })
      );
      const token = cookies["access_session"];
      if (!token) return false;
      try {
        const decoded = Buffer.from(decodeURIComponent(token), "base64").toString("utf8");
        const parts = decoded.split(".");
        if (parts.length !== 3) return false;
        const [userId, expiresAtStr] = parts;     // ← parts[2] (signature) IGNORED
        const expiresAt = parseInt(expiresAtStr, 10);
        if (isNaN(expiresAt) || Date.now() > expiresAt) return false;
        // در middleware نمی‌تونیم HMAC رو verify کنیم چون SESSION_SECRET
        // بهش دسترسی نداریم
        // فقط ساختار رو چک می‌کنیم — API route اصلی خودش HMAC رو verify می‌کنه
        return userId.length > 0;                  // ← only format check
      } catch {
        return false;
      }
    }
  Analysis:
    The session token format (defined in access-auth.ts:67-72,
    createSessionToken) is:
      payload = `${userId}.${expiresAt}`
      sig     = hmac(payload)            // sha256(SESSION_SECRET, payload)
      token   = base64(`${payload}.${sig}`)
    Middleware NEVER verifies `sig` (parts[2]). It only checks:
      (a) parts.length === 3
      (b) expiresAt is a number and not in the past
      (c) userId is non-empty (any string passes, even "x")
    An attacker who knows (or guesses) any valid cuid userId can forge
    a cookie that passes middleware's session gate:
      forged = base64(`${victimUserId}.${futureTs}.${anyGarbage}`)
    The comment at lines 87-88 explicitly admits this and relies on the
    API layer (access-auth.ts:78-96 verifySessionToken, which uses
    crypto.timingSafeEqual) as the real check.
  Defense-in-depth impact:
    - All /api/admin/* requests that pass middleware's session gate
      still reach the API route handler. There, checkAdminAuth
      (admin-auth.ts:17-31) / checkAdminSession (admin-session.ts:11-24)
      call getSessionFromRequest (access-auth.ts:186-201) →
      verifySessionToken REJECTS the forged signature. ✅ Today's
      admin endpoints are still safe.
    - BUT: any admin route that forgets to call checkAdminAuth/
      checkAdminSession (or any future route added without it) becomes
      exploitable up to the 24h expiry window. Defense-in-depth is
      broken at the middleware layer.
    - WORSE: the /user-dashboard PAGE GATE at lines 180-185 uses ONLY
      hasValidSession. A forged cookie causes the BROWSER to render
      the /user-dashboard page (client-side fetches will then 401, but
      the page shell, layout, any static content embedded in the page
      itself, and any client-only data is exposed). This is a page-gate
      bypass, not just a defense-in-depth gap.
    - Additional DoS vector: forged cookies reach API handlers; each
      request burns a db.accessUser.findUnique call (admin-auth.ts:23)
      before being rejected. Combined with the lack of rate limit on
      /api/admin/* (F-5 still open), this is a cheap DB-cost DoS.
  Cross-reference: F-1 in prior audit (still open).
  Severity: HIGH
  PoC (page-gate bypass):
    # Attacker does NOT need SESSION_SECRET. Just needs to know/guess
    # a cuid userId (24-char base36, not enumerable but leakable via
    # logs, referrer, source maps, etc.):
    USERID="cm1234567890abcdefghijk"     # any plausible cuid
    FUTURE=$((($(date +%s)+3600)*1000))
    PAYLOAD="${USERID}.${FUTURE}.deadbeef"   # fake sig
    TOKEN=$(printf '%s' "$PAYLOAD" | base64)
    curl -s "https://victim.com/user-dashboard" \
      -H "Cookie: access_session=${TOKEN}" | head -c 200
    # → HTTP 200 with /user-dashboard HTML (instead of 302 redirect to
    #   /user-login). The page renders. Client-side fetches will 401,
    #   but the page shell + any embedded static content is exposed.
  PoC (resource-waste DoS):
    # Forged cookies reach API handlers; each request burns a DB lookup
    # before being rejected:
    while true; do
      curl -s -o /dev/null "https://victim.com/api/admin/users" \
        -H "Cookie: access_session=${TOKEN}"
    done
    # → no rate limit on /api/admin/* (F-5), each request hits DB.
